Write a function in PascalABC.NET to find the area of a triangle given the lengths of all three sides. The function should validate that the given side lengths form a valid triangle before calculating the area. If the side lengths do not form a valid triangle, the function should throw an exception with an appropriate error message.

In addition, the function should also check if the triangle is equilateral, isosceles, or scalene. If the triangle is equilateral, the function should return a string stating "Equilateral triangle". If the triangle is isosceles, the function should return a string stating "Isosceles triangle". If the triangle is scalene, the function should return a string stating "Scalene triangle".

The function should have a time complexity of O(1) and a space complexity of O(1).

Each string must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one special character (such as @, #, $, etc.). Print out each string, but replace all uppercase letters with lowercase letters and vice versa. Additionally, sort the strings in descending order based on the number of special characters present in each string. 

Note: The program should handle edge cases where the number of strings is less than or equal to zero, or if the user provides an invalid input for N.

Here's the code to create a ranking system for 20 players based on their scores in PascalABC.NET:

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

class Program
{
    static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        Dictionary<string, int> players = new Dictionary<string, int>()
        {
            { "Player1", 65 },
            { "Player2", 82 },
            { "Player3", 47 },
            { "Player4", 79 },
            { "Player5", 65 },
            { "Player6", 74 },
            { "Player7", 53 },
            { "Player8", 91 },
            { "Player9", 63 },
            { "Player10", 82 },
            { "Player11", 87 },
            { "Player12", 77 },
            { "Player13", 82 },
            { "Player14", 92 },
            { "Player15", 58 },
            { "Player16", 70 },
            { "Player17", 80 },
            { "Player18", 82 },
            { "Player19", 76 },
            { "Player20", 90 }
        };

        // Sort players by score in descending order
        List<KeyValuePair<string, int>> sortedPlayers = players.ToList();
        sortedPlayers.Sort((x, y) => y.Value.CompareTo(x.Value));

        Console.WriteLine("Rank | Player   | Score");
        Console.WriteLine("----------------------");

        int rank = 1;
        foreach (KeyValuePair<string, int> player in sortedPlayers)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"{rank,4} | {player.Key,-8} | {player.Value,4}");
            rank++;
        }
    }
}
```
